speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have knee pain after increasing your physical activity. To help narrow this down, on a scale of 1 to 10, how severe is the pain, and does it worsen with weight-bearing or at rest? Also, have you noticed any swelling, redness, or an audible 'pop' when the pain started?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the combination of pivoting movements and sudden onset is concerning. Did you feel or hear a distinct "pop" at the moment of injury, and is the pain specifically localized to the front of your knee or the joint line? Also, is your knee currently locking, catching, or giving way when you walk?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Plica Syndrome. Given the pain location over the medial aspect of the tibia and worsening with activity, I request images of the knee to confirm plica thickening or entrapment. REQUEST IMAGES: Knee_MRI_Coronal
